desc:
React Native app development for iOS and Android lets you launch on both phones from one codebase. Ecom Swift LLC builds your app from a brief or sketches, tests it on real devices and prepares store-ready builds in your own Apple and Google developer accounts.

## What is React Native app development?

React Native is a framework that lets one team write an app in JavaScript or TypeScript and run it as a real native app on iPhone and Android. The screens you see are built from native interface parts, so the app feels at home on each phone. You keep one project, one set of features and one place to fix bugs.

For a founder or small business, this means a mobile app does not have to cost twice as much or take twice as long. You still publish two separate store listings, but the work behind them is shared.

## Why does one codebase matter for a new app?

Two separate native apps mean two teams, two sets of bugs and two release schedules. Every new feature has to be built, tested and explained twice. Small companies often run out of budget before the second app is finished, and half of their customers wait.

A shared codebase keeps both versions in step. When you change a button label, a price screen or a sign-up rule, the change reaches iPhone and Android users together. That also makes handover simpler, because a future developer reads one project instead of two.

## How the build quality shapes installs and retention

People judge an app in its first minute. If the first screen is slow, the buttons are hard to tap or the app crashes on an older phone, they delete it and rarely come back. A clean first run, quick screen changes and clear error messages keep people inside the app long enough to see its value.

Good structure matters later too. When screens, data calls and navigation follow clear patterns, new features are cheaper to add and fewer bugs appear after each update. Many outcomes depend on your idea, your market and your marketing, so we focus on what we control: a stable, tidy app that is easy to improve.

## What a great React Native app includes

- A written screen list agreed before any code is written.
- Navigation that follows iOS and Android habits, including the Android back button.
- Your brand colors, fonts and icons applied consistently across every screen.
- Sign in and user accounts where the idea needs them.
- A backend or Firebase connection with clear loading, empty and error states.
- Push notifications set up with permission asked at a sensible moment.
- Analytics and crash reporting, so you learn how people use the app.
- Builds tested on real iPhones and Android phones, not only simulators.
- A repository you own, with a build guide for the next developer.
- Store listing drafts, screenshots and a submission checklist.

## What we do

We begin by turning your idea, sketches or rough notes into a screen list and a short feature description that you approve in writing. Nothing is built until that list is clear.

Next we set up the project, build the screens and connect your data. The Basic package covers a small, polished app with one core feature working end to end. Standard adds accounts, a backend and push notifications. Premium adds payments or subscriptions, analytics and help with submission.

We test on real devices, fix what we find and prepare builds in your developer accounts. You receive the source code in your own repository, a build guide and a store submission checklist.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Describe the one thing a user should be able to do on day one.
- Share any sketches, competitor apps or screenshots you like.
- Decide early whether people need accounts to use the app.
- Test the build on your own phone and note what feels slow.
- Plan for store review time before any launch date.

**Avoid:**
- Packing the whole wish list into the first release.
- Choosing a backend only because a friend suggested it.
- Skipping crash reporting, which leaves you blind after launch.
- Copying another app's screens and wording too closely.
- Assuming a store will accept the app without checking its rules.

## Who this service is for

A founder with a clear idea and no technical team can use this to get a working app without hiring a developer full time. A small business that already has a website may want an app for bookings, orders or loyalty. An agency may need a reliable builder for a client project and prefer to hand over a clean repository.

## What we need from you

Send your idea, sketches or a short brief, plus your logo, brand colors and any example apps you like. You will need your own Apple and Google developer accounts for store release, and we can guide you through opening them. We never need your passwords. Access is given as a team member or developer user, and we reply with a short checklist after you order.
